title: Quickwire: session resume micro-API prototyping log
content:
Goal:
- Fast, low-cost session resume for conversational apps (mobile + web) where users re-enter within short windows (seconds to minutes).
- Surface: tiny API that returns a compact resume token + warmed routing hints so hosted runtime can reduce first-response latency and token cost.

Why Quickwire? (intuition)
- Many apps lose prompt context on short navigations or backgrounding; re-sending full context is expensive.
- Prefix/KV warmup and small deltas can cut perc-token cost and warm latency dramatically.
- Product win: perceived responsiveness + lower host token spend for typical chat flows.

Non-goals (for v0)
- Full persistent conversation store, long-term retention, or cross-device sync.
- Complex privacy flows (we will defer to Private/RPC product).

V0 proposal (sketch)
- New endpoint: POST /v1/sessions/quickwire-resume
  - payload: { session_id, user_id (optional), last_active_ts, resume_budget_tokens (opt), fidelity_hint }
  - response: { resume_token, kv_slot_hints, warm_hint_version, estimated_extra_latency_ms }
- Internals: platform stores ephemeral compact snapshots (vector of recent token hashes + small semantic fingerprint) for N seconds (configurable per org). Resume_token is opaque JWT-style reference that maps to a RAM-backed snapshot.
- Runtime: when resume_token used for next Generate/Chat call, router prioritizes pulling KV cache and placing request into a warmed lane (fast-path), skipping some cold-start steps.

User stories
- U1 (mobile chat): As a mobile user who backgrounds the app for 12s, I want the assistant to respond quickly when I reopen the chat without the app re-sending a 2KB prompt.
- U2 (email thread): As a user switching tabs, I want my draft assistant reply to be resumed with minimal lag so I can continue editing.
- U3 (high-throughput bot): As a customer with many short interactions per session, I want per-interaction token costs reduced by avoiding repeated prefix tokens.

Success metrics (what we'll measure)
- SLO: median extra latency attributable to resume < 80ms for warmed requests (target 50ms).
- Cost: average per-interaction prompt token delta reduced by >= 20% on resumed flows.
- Uptake: percent of resumed flows using Quickwire token within 1st week of rollout >= 10% of sessions with short gap (<60s).
- Quality: no degradation in model output for resumed vs full-prefix baselines (auto-eval pass rate >= 98%).

Telemetry / signals to track
- resume_token issuance rate, expiry distribution
- hit rate on quickwire warm lane vs fallback cold path
- extra latency breakdown (routing, kv-read, kernel warm)
- token delta histogram (resumed vs full context)
- errors: token-miss, stale-token, auth-fail

Experiment matrix (alpha)
- E1 (time window): keep snapshots for 15s / 60s / 300s — measure hit rate and memory cost.
- E2 (snapshot granularity): compact fingerprint (hashes + small vector) vs near-full short prefix (first 128 tokens) — tradeoff accuracy vs storage.
- E3 (fidelity_hint modes): "minimal" (only essential instruction set), "full" (full prefix), "adaptive" (server decides) — track quality regressions.

Operational constraints / safety
- Snapshot TTL per-org and global upper bound (default 60s, max 24h gated via enterprise config).
- Snapshot redaction: drop user PII, API keys, and attachments before storing. Provide opt-out header for customers who want no resume.
- Auth: resume_token bound to account/org and short-lived (rotating signing key).

Edge cases / open questions
- Q1: Do we allow session resume across devices? (cross-device probably requires persistent storage & explicit consent) -> avoid in v0.
- Q2: How to handle model-rollover or quantization changes making warm hints stale? -> include warm_hint_version and provide graceful fallback to cold path.
- Q3: Billing model for resumed flows: bill tokens for the eventual model call only; but we may want a tiny fixed price for Quickwire metadata usage. Need finance input.

Implementation plan (milestones)
- Week 0–2: minimal storage shims + opaque token generator; basic API + auth checks (internal-only).
- Week 2–4: runtime integration: warm-path routing with kv slot hints; simulate cold vs warm lanes locally.
- Week 4–6: alpha rollout to 1 org (internal teams) + telemetry dashboard.
- Week 6–8: iterate experiments E1/E2/E3, fix quality regressions, add opt-out header.

Dev notes / TODOs
- [ ] Spike: memory cost model for snapshot TTLs (Ravi)
- [ ] Security review checklist itemize (Ellie)
- [ ] Draft API contract + sample SDK snippets (Marcus)
- [ ] Quick local perf harness for cold->warm latency (writebench)

Sketch: naive resume flow
1) Client calls /sessions/quickwire-resume -> platform returns resume_token (store ephemeral snapshot).
2) Client immediately issues chat.generate with resume_token in header: X-Resume-Token.
3) Router sees token, performs fast kv warm using snapshot hints, places request on warmed worker pool.
4) If warm step fails or token invalid, fallback: route to normal cold path and record metric.

Minimal SDK example (pseudocode)
- python:
  token = client.sessions.quickwire.create(session_id)
  resp = client.chat.generate(
    session_id=session_id,
    resume_token=token,
    messages=[...]    
  )

Acceptance criteria for v0 demo
- demo chat where reopening after 20s shows <80ms extra latency vs continuous session baseline.
- dashboard shows basic telemetry + flagged regressions (if any).

Notes to self: keep this lean. The biggest wins are short TTLs and compact fingerprints. Avoid early optimism about cross-device sync. Need a quick call with infra about ephemeral RAM-backed keys and SRE about eviction strategy.

Links / references (internal)

- threading: #session-quickwire in product slack thread (see March 1st thread)

End of log (for now).
